John Dryden (1631–1700).  The Poems of John Dryden.  1913.

Songs from the Plays

“Your Hay it is Mow’d, and your Corn is Reap’d,” from 
King Arthur

Comus.
Your Hay it is Mow’d, and your Corn is Reap’d;
Your Barns will be full, and your Hovels heap’d:
Come, my Boys, come;
Come, my Boys, come;
And merrily Roar out Harvest Home.
Chorus.
Come, my Boys, come, &c.
1 
Man.
W
E
 ha’ cheated the Parson, we’ll cheat him agen,
For why shou’d a Blockhead ha’ One in Ten?
One in Ten,
One in Ten,
For why shou’d a Blockhead ha’ One in Ten?
2For Prating so long like a Book-learn’d Sot,
Till Pudding and Dumplin burn to Pot,
Burn to Pot,
Burn to Pot,
Till Pudding and Dumplin burn to Pot.
Chorus.
Burn to Pot, &c.

And Hoigh for the Honour of old
